metadata.workload: weak scaling: each worker performs K increments, total work P*K
metadata.timing: parent start-event release to latest worker finish; spawn, compilation, and process exit excluded; event wakeup and privatized final locked write included
metadata.aggregation: median over repeats; each variant uses its own P=1 median baseline
metadata.karp_flatt_interpretation: The assignment requests this formula despite fixed K per worker. These are NOT strong-scaling serial-fraction estimates: ideal weak scaling yields e_requested=1, not 0.
metadata.throughput_speedup_formula: S_throughput = P * T1 / Tp; weak_scaling_efficiency = T1 / Tp
measurement_caveats: Native volatile C loops, not Python interpreted increments; every shared increment reads and writes memory.
Counters are aligned; unpadded P<=8 fits within the first 64 bytes. padded uses at least one detected hardware cache line.
padded_64 is additionally reported when the detected line differs from 64 bytes; 64-byte strides do not isolate a 128-byte line.
RawArray is lock-free in the hot loop; privatized uses one lock only for each worker's final publication.
OS scheduling, heterogeneous cores, power management, and unrelated load can affect measurements; no observed collapse is assumed or fabricated.
Very short native loops may be dominated by event wakeup; inspect repeat spread and per-worker native loop times.
